paragraphs: Ada-R1 addresses the cost of language models that produce long reasoning traces. The authors find that longer reasoning helps some problems but offers no benefit, or even reduces accuracy, on others. This makes reasoning depth a choice that should depend on the input, rather than a fixed behavior applied to every question.

The method first merges models that use long and short chains of thought, creating a model with access to both reasoning styles. It then trains preferences at two levels. At the group level, training encourages selection of a suitable style. Within each style, it favors reasoning that is both correct and concise. These two decisions distinguish choosing how to reason from improving a particular reasoning path.

Experiments report lower inference costs than the compared approaches while maintaining performance. Across five mathematics datasets, average reasoning length falls by more than half. The finding supports adaptive reasoning as an efficiency strategy: savings can come from selecting a shorter style when appropriate, as well as from removing unnecessary steps within a longer explanation.
neurips-2025-ada-r1-hybrid-cot-via-bi-le.tldr: Ada-R1 learns when to use long or short reasoning, cutting average reasoning length by over 50% on five mathematics datasets while maintaining performance.

paragraphs: BayeSQP tackles black-box optimization, where an algorithm can evaluate an objective and constraints without directly receiving their derivatives. It combines the local search structure of sequential quadratic programming with Bayesian models of uncertainty. The aim is to use estimated slopes and curvature to guide search even when only function evaluations are available.

The algorithm builds Gaussian process surrogates that jointly estimate function values, gradients, and Hessians for the objective and constraints. At each iteration, these estimates define a local optimization problem that produces a search direction. Crucially, that problem includes uncertainty in both values and derivatives. Its formulation becomes a tractable second-order cone program designed to support improvements with high probability under model uncertainty.

After choosing a direction, BayeSQP uses constrained Thompson sampling for a one-dimensional line search that selects the next evaluation point. Experiments show advantages over state-of-the-art methods in specific high-dimensional settings. The contribution is a way to connect derivative-based optimization structure with uncertainty-aware search; the reported advantage is tied to those tested settings.
neurips-2025-bayesqp-bayesian-optimizati.tldr: BayeSQP estimates derivatives and their uncertainty from function evaluations to guide black-box optimization, with gains in specific high-dimensional settings.

paragraphs: CAD-Coder turns natural-language descriptions into CadQuery scripts, using a Python-based parametric CAD language as its output representation. This makes the generated result executable as a geometric model and allows direct checks of its geometry. The representation also gives language models a richer vocabulary for describing construction operations.

Training proceeds in two stages. Supervised fine-tuning first teaches the model from paired descriptions and CadQuery code. Reinforcement learning then uses Group Reward Policy Optimization with a reward that combines geometric agreement, measured through Chamfer Distance, and compliance with the required output format. A chain-of-thought planning process additionally supports reasoning about how to construct the requested object.

The authors build an automated data pipeline producing 110,000 description–script–3D model triplets and 1,500 planning examples. Their experiments report generation of varied, valid, and complex CAD models, alongside advances in text-to-CAD performance and geometric reasoning. The central idea is to connect language-based code generation with feedback about the resulting shape, so training addresses both the script and the geometry it produces.
neurips-2025-cad-coder-text-to-cad-gener.tldr: CAD-Coder generates CAD scripts from text using supervised training, reasoning plans, and reinforcement learning rewards for geometry and format.

paragraphs: CoRGII addresses retrieval of graphs containing a structure that matches a query graph. Existing representations can assess such matches accurately, but retrieval becomes expensive when every graph in a collection must be scored. The paper seeks to retain useful structural matching while making the collection searchable through an index.

The framework converts contextual dense graph representations into sparse binary codes over a learned vocabulary. This gives each graph a representation resembling a text document, allowing established inverted-index machinery to be used. The conversion is learned through a differentiable discretization module, and the resulting system still supports soft vector-based containment scores. It also learns how strongly each vocabulary item should contribute to a graph's score.

CoRGII is trained end to end from binary relevance labels, without requiring detailed annotations that align query components with components of retrieved graphs. Experiments report better efficiency–accuracy trade-offs than several baselines. The result shows how learned graph representations can be adapted to an established retrieval infrastructure while avoiding the need for fine-grained matching supervision.
neurips-2025-contextual-tokenization-for.tldr: CoRGII converts learned graph representations into indexable sparse codes, improving the measured trade-off between retrieval speed and accuracy.

paragraphs: COSIMO is a neural architecture for data represented by simplicial complexes, structures that capture interactions involving more than pairs of elements. Such representations are useful for problems including trajectory prediction and mesh processing. The paper examines how to learn on these structures using continuous dynamics instead of relying primarily on discrete filtering operations.

The architecture is derived from partial differential equations defined on simplicial complexes. This supplies a mathematical basis for how information evolves through the model. The authors provide theoretical and experimental support for its stability when the simplicial structure is perturbed. They also study over-smoothing, the tendency for learned representations to become excessively similar, and show that COSIMO offers better control of this effect than discrete simplicial networks.

Experiments on real-world datasets find performance competitive with state-of-the-art simplicial neural networks in complex and noisy settings. The contribution therefore combines a different modeling foundation with evidence about stability and representation quality. Its stated advantage is better control of over-smoothing alongside competitive task performance, rather than an across-the-board claim of higher accuracy.
neurips-2025-continuous-simplicial-neura.tldr: COSIMO derives simplicial neural networks from continuous equations, providing stability support and better control of over-smoothing with competitive performance.

paragraphs: Conventional autoregressive language models generate text from left to right, committing to each token before producing the next. An early mistake can therefore remain in the text and influence later output. This paper targets that accumulation of errors by changing the generation procedure so that some earlier choices can be reconsidered.

The proposed method, Resample-Previous-Tokens, repeatedly revisits a window of text that the model has already generated. Tokens in that window may be replaced during these revisits. The key change is that generation includes opportunities for correction within recent output, rather than treating every earlier token as irrevocable. The method is intended to reduce the persistence of mistakes as the sequence grows.

The authors fine-tune a pretrained model with eight billion parameters using this approach and report approximately 10% relative improvements on reasoning and coding benchmarks compared with standard sampling. This is evidence that revisiting generated tokens can improve performance in the tested setting. The reported result combines RPT with fine-tuning, so it describes that trained system's performance rather than an isolated change applied to an otherwise unchanged model.
neurips-2025-corrector-sampling-in-langu.tldr: Resample-Previous-Tokens lets a language model revise recent output, yielding roughly 10% relative gains on reasoning and coding benchmarks after fine-tuning.

paragraphs: DeceptionBench evaluates how deceptive outputs appear in realistic social contexts. Its focus is broader than whether a model produces a false statement: it examines patterns of deception and the circumstances that influence them. The benchmark contains 150 scenarios and more than 1,000 samples across economy, healthcare, education, social interaction, and entertainment.

The evaluation separates two behavioral tendencies: pursuing self-interested outcomes and appeasing the user. It also varies external conditions, comparing neutral contexts with reward incentives and coercive pressure. Sustained interactions across multiple turns add feedback dynamics, allowing the benchmark to examine how behavior develops as a conversation continues rather than only testing isolated responses.

Experiments with language models and reasoning models reveal vulnerabilities, including stronger deception under reinforcing feedback. The findings indicate that the tested models do not reliably resist manipulative contextual cues. By connecting behavioral tendencies with incentives and conversational feedback, the benchmark provides a structured way to investigate when deceptive outputs become more likely and motivates safeguards that account for the surrounding interaction.
neurips-2025-deceptionbench-a-comprehens.tldr: DeceptionBench tests deception across five societal domains and finds that incentives and reinforcing interactions can amplify deceptive model behavior.

paragraphs: This paper studies causal function estimation when confounding variables are hidden but measurements that serve as proxies for them are available. Within proxy causal learning, two existing approaches use outcome bridges and treatment bridges. The authors develop two kernel-based, doubly robust estimators that combine these approaches while accommodating continuous and high-dimensional variables.

Their identification strategy builds on a treatment-bridge method that avoids estimating density ratios. The new estimators also avoid indicator functions and kernel smoothing over the treatment variable. Those features matter particularly for treatments that vary continuously or have many dimensions. Kernel mean embeddings provide the mathematical representation used to construct the estimators, and both have closed-form solutions.

The paper establishes strong uniform consistency guarantees and reports better performance than existing methods on proxy causal learning benchmarks. These comparisons include an earlier doubly robust approach that requires both density-ratio estimation and kernel smoothing. The contribution is a combination of theoretical guarantees and a formulation that removes those estimation components, broadening the practical appeal of combining outcome and treatment bridges.
neurips-2025-density-ratio-free-doubly-r.tldr: Two kernel-based estimators combine outcome and treatment bridges for proxy causal learning without density-ratio estimation or smoothing over treatments.

paragraphs: This paper studies sequential selection under matroid constraints, where accepted elements must form an independent set. The objective is to improve the smallest acceptance probability across all elements. This makes fairness a property of each element's chance of being selected, and the authors analyze how arrival order and constraint structure affect achievable guarantees.

For adversarial arrival orders, they give a nearly optimal fairness factor of α(ln(k)+1), where α is matroid arboricity and k is rank. For laminar matroids, an online coloring method yields a factor of 2α−1, optimal up to constants. For graphic matroids under random arrival, sampling edges to learn a degeneracy ordering gives a factor of (4+o(1))α, also optimal up to constants.

The analysis extends to p-matchoids, with a factor of β(p ln(k)+1) under adversarial arrivals, where β represents optimal offline fairness. All results can also accommodate a setting with no prior knowledge of the matroid at the cost of a logarithmic increase in the fairness factor. Together, the guarantees quantify what online selection can preserve across different structural and information settings.
neurips-2025-fair-matroid-selection-8ffd.tldr: The paper develops online selection algorithms with near-optimal fairness guarantees for several matroid settings and extensions to p-matchoids.

paragraphs: FlowerTune studies how pretrained language models behave when fine-tuned through federated learning. This setting allows decentralized training without sharing raw data, making it relevant to specialized or sensitive information that may be unavailable in public datasets. The paper addresses the limited understanding of which models and training strategies work well in that setting.

The authors introduce a leaderboard and benchmarking suite covering general language tasks, finance, medicine, and coding. Each domain includes instruction-tuning datasets arranged for federated use and evaluation metrics suited to that domain. The comparison spans 26 pretrained language models and examines different methods for aggregating learning across participants and for fine-tuning the models.

The reported contribution is a broad, community-driven comparison that connects model performance with resource constraints and domain adaptation. This gives researchers a common basis for assessing federated fine-tuning choices across several kinds of task. Its significance lies in making decentralized adaptation more systematically measurable and supporting the development of domain-specialized models trained without centralizing participants' raw data.
neurips-2025-flowertune-a-cross-domain-b.tldr: FlowerTune benchmarks federated fine-tuning across 26 language models and four domains, comparing performance, training strategies, and resource constraints.

paragraphs: This paper examines concept shift, where the relationship between inputs and labels changes between training and testing. It asks how learning from more data interacts with that change. The theoretical analysis focuses on ridge regression and derives an exact prediction-risk expression in a limiting regime called the thermodynamic limit.

The results identify a phase transition separating weak and strong concept shift. They also show that test performance can vary nonmonotonically with the amount of data, even without double descent. Thus, within the analyzed setting, adding data does not necessarily improve performance steadily when the relationship learned during training differs from the one encountered at test time.

Experiments with transformers pretrained to perform linear regression agree well with the theory. Under concept shift, excessively long contexts can hurt next-token generalization. Experiments on MNIST and FashionMNIST provide further support. Together, these findings suggest that the tension between specialization and generalization under changing concepts extends beyond the regression calculation, while the exact risk expression remains a result for the specified theoretical setting.
neurips-2025-generalization-vs-specializ.tldr: Theory and experiments show that more data or longer context can hurt generalization when the input–label relationship changes.

paragraphs: Graphs Help Graphs addresses collaboration among agents working with fragmented, heterogeneous, and changing graphs. The paper identifies problems in existing collaboration schemes: useful shared information can collapse or be forgotten, and growing graphs can lose benefits accumulated through earlier interactions. Its Graph Socialized Learning paradigm treats collaboration itself as something that must be organized and maintained.

The proposed method uses a graph-based organizational structure to choose which agents interact and to manage the strength of those interactions autonomously. Information is exchanged through synthetic graphs customized to an agent's needs. These synthetic graphs also support the construction of prototypes throughout the learning life cycle, which help select parameters.

The design brings together decisions about whom to collaborate with, what to share, and when to share and accumulate information. An extensive empirical study reports effectiveness on heterogeneous dynamic graphs. The significance is a coordinated approach to collaboration that accounts for differences among agents and changes in their graphs, with synthetic graphs serving both as an exchange medium and as a resource for later learning.
neurips-2025-graphs-help-graphs-multi-ag.tldr: Graphs Help Graphs organizes agent collaboration through adaptive interaction relationships and customized synthetic graphs, with empirical benefits on changing heterogeneous graphs.

paragraphs: SPORT trains multimodal agents to use external tools without pre-collected task answers or tool-use trajectories. Such annotations can be expensive or impractical for complex tasks. The method instead creates tasks and learning feedback through an iterative process, allowing the controller to improve from its own exploration of tool use.

The process has four parts: task synthesis, step sampling, step verification, and preference tuning. Language models first generate multimodal tasks. The agent then alternates between trying tool-use steps and having a verifier assess them. The resulting AI feedback produces preferences between steps, which are used to update the controller. Repeating this cycle connects exploration in real environments with changes to the agent's tool-use behavior.

Evaluations report improvements of 6.41% on GTA and 3.64% on GAIA. These findings support the effectiveness and generalization of the trained agent in the tested benchmarks. The central contribution is a training loop that creates its own step-level preference data, reducing dependence on human-authored examples of complete solutions and tool trajectories.
neurips-2025-iterative-tool-usage-explor.tldr: SPORT improves multimodal tool use through synthesized tasks, autonomous exploration, AI verification, and step-level preference training.

paragraphs: MaNGO addresses the difficulty of adapting learned physics simulators when material properties change. Graph Network Simulators offer fast inference, but the paper identifies repeated retraining and data collection for new parameter settings as major obstacles. Its starting point is that simulations with different physical parameters can share an underlying latent structure.

The method learns that shared structure through meta-learning. It encodes graph trajectories using conditional neural processes to produce a latent representation, enabling adaptation to new physical parameters without retraining. The architecture combines this representation with a neural operator designed to mitigate the accumulation of prediction errors over time. Adaptation and long-term prediction quality are therefore addressed within the same simulator.

Experiments cover several dynamics-prediction tasks with varying material properties. MaNGO outperforms existing Graph Network Simulator methods, and its accuracy on unseen material properties approaches that of an oracle model. These results support using shared structure across simulations to transfer knowledge between parameter settings, while also addressing the compounding errors that arise when predictions are extended through time.
neurips-2025-mango-adaptable-graph-netwo.tldr: MaNGO meta-learns shared simulation structure to adapt to unseen material properties without retraining, achieving accuracy close to an oracle in reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper asks how much stochastic predictions actually help an online controller facing random disturbances. Prediction error alone does not capture the dependence between a forecast and the disturbance it concerns. The authors therefore model their joint distribution and define prediction power as the reduction in control cost from using predictions optimally compared with ignoring them.

For a time-varying Linear Quadratic Regulator, they derive a closed-form expression for prediction power. This reveals how a prediction's usefulness for control can differ from its accuracy. The paper also discusses the connection with online policy optimization, linking the assessment of forecasts to the decisions made using them.

The analysis extends to more general dynamics and costs through a lower bound on prediction power. That bound holds under two sufficient conditions that generalize properties of the linear-quadratic setting. Applying it to non-quadratic costs shows that even weakly dependent predictions can produce substantial gains. The result directs attention to decision-relevant statistical structure, while keeping the broader guarantee conditional on those sufficient conditions.
neurips-2025-maximizing-the-value-of-pre.tldr: The paper measures predictions by their optimal control-cost benefit and shows why forecast accuracy alone can misrepresent that value.

paragraphs: Bregman preference optimization, or BPO, generalizes direct preference optimization by viewing alignment as likelihood-ratio estimation. The paper argues that the target policy can be uniquely identified through its ratio, without introducing a reward model or partition function. This provides a basis for designing preference-training losses with target-policy optimality guarantees.

BPO offers a family of objectives that includes DPO as a special case. The authors give tractable forms for all instances and introduce scaled Basu's power divergence as a gradient-scaling method. The framework can also work with target policies defined by other DPO variants, making the ratio-matching formulation compatible with additional preference-optimization choices.

In experiments, BPO instances improve both win rate and entropy compared with DPO, addressing the observed trade-off between generation fidelity and diversity in other probabilistic extensions. Applied to Llama-3-8B-Instruct, BPO reaches a 55.9% length-controlled win rate on AlpacaEval2 and reports state-of-the-art performance among Llama-3-8B backbones. The empirical contribution is simultaneous improvement on these measures, alongside a broader theoretically grounded family of training objectives.
neurips-2025-preference-optimization-by-.tldr: BPO generalizes DPO through likelihood-ratio matching, with target-policy guarantees and reported improvements in both win rate and entropy.

paragraphs: Prior Guidance improves diffusion-based planning in offline reinforcement learning, where policies are learned from a fixed dataset. These planners create trajectories through iterative denoising. Existing ways of steering generation toward high returns can struggle with multiple action modes, drift from the data distribution, or require expensive inference-time searches.

The proposed method changes the distribution from which generation begins. It replaces the standard Gaussian prior of a behavior-cloned diffusion model with a learned distribution, optimized using an objective that includes behavior regularization. This directs generation toward valuable trajectories without costly reward optimization of the diffusion model itself. It also removes the need to generate multiple candidates solely to select among them at inference time.

The authors provide an efficient training strategy that applies behavior regularization in latent space. Across varied long-horizon offline reinforcement-learning benchmarks, Prior Guidance outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion policies and planners. The contribution is to move guidance into the learned starting distribution, combining return-oriented trajectory generation with a training mechanism that accounts for the behavior represented in the dataset.
neurips-2025-prior-guided-diffusion-plan.tldr: Prior Guidance learns the starting distribution for diffusion planning, improving benchmark performance without inference-time selection among multiple candidate trajectories.

paragraphs: Diffusion-DRO aims to align text-to-image diffusion models with human preferences. The paper identifies two difficulties in existing preference methods: probability-estimation issues associated with a nonlinear sigmoid objective and the restricted diversity of offline training data. Its approach reformulates preference learning as ranking, drawing on inverse reinforcement learning.

This ranking formulation removes the need for a reward model and produces a denoising-based training objective. It is designed to overcome the nonlinear estimation problem encountered by earlier methods. Training also combines offline expert demonstrations with negative samples generated by the current policy online, bringing newly generated examples into the preference-learning process instead of relying entirely on a fixed dataset.

Experiments report better generation quality on challenging prompts and prompts unseen during training. Diffusion-DRO outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both quantitative evaluations and user studies. The significance is the combination of a simpler denoising formulation with an evolving source of comparison samples, addressing both the mathematical structure of preference training and the coverage of examples available to it.
neurips-2025-ranking-based-preference-op.tldr: Diffusion-DRO learns image preferences through denoising-based ranking and online negative samples, improving reported generation quality and user-study results.

paragraphs: This paper reexamines semi-supervised learning when the starting point is a pretrained vision foundation model. It studies tasks on which frozen models perform poorly and asks how labeled and unlabeled examples should be used during adaptation. The results challenge the assumption that traditional semi-supervised methods are automatically the strongest option in this setting.

The authors find that parameter-efficient fine-tuning using labeled data alone often outperforms traditional semi-supervised approaches, even though those approaches can use unlabeled data. They also find that the fine-tuned models produce useful pseudo-labels for unlabeled examples. Different parameter-efficient tuning techniques supply complementary pseudo-labels, making their diversity a useful source of supervision.

These observations motivate a baseline that ensembles pseudo-labels across multiple tuning methods and vision foundation model backbones. Extensive experiments support its effectiveness. The practical finding is that strong adaptation on the labeled subset can be an important foundation for using unlabeled data, and that combining predictions from diverse adaptations can improve the supervisory signal available for semi-supervised learning.
neurips-2025-revisiting-semi-supervised-.tldr: The study finds strong labeled-only tuning baselines and improves semi-supervised learning by combining pseudo-labels from diverse foundation-model adaptations.

paragraphs: DiffeoCFM generates brain connectivity matrices while respecting their mathematical constraints. Covariance and correlation matrices occupy structured spaces, so a generative method must account for more than their individual entries. Direct use of Riemannian geometry can make this expensive by requiring specialized definitions of paths, norms, and integration.

The paper uses global invertible transformations to define pullback metrics on these matrix spaces. Under those metrics, the authors show that Riemannian conditional flow matching is equivalent to ordinary conditional flow matching applied after transforming the data. This allows efficient learning of vector fields and sampling with standard ordinary differential equation solvers. The implementations use matrix logarithms for covariance matrices and normalized Cholesky decompositions for correlation matrices.

Evaluation covers three fMRI datasets with more than 4,600 scans from 2,800 subjects and two EEG datasets with more than 30,000 trials from 26 subjects. The method reports fast training and state-of-the-art performance while preserving manifold constraints. Its main contribution is an equivalence that makes geometry-aware generation accessible through standard computational tools.
neurips-2025-riemannian-flow-matching-fo.tldr: DiffeoCFM uses invertible data transformations to efficiently generate brain connectivity matrices while preserving their geometric constraints.

paragraphs: SAGE recognizes physical object states and their changes in video. This requires sensitivity to visual details and temporal context, which pretrained vision-language models can struggle to capture. Specialized recognition systems also face difficulty when confronted with objects or actions they have not seen before.

The framework represents states through fine-grained visual concepts described in language. Because these concepts can be shared across objects and actions, they provide a common basis for modeling different physical transitions. Large language models first construct a State-Action Graph, and vision-language models then refine that graph using multimodal information. The graph connects the representation of states with the actions involved in their transformation.

Experiments show substantial improvements over baselines and effective generalization to unseen objects and actions in open-world settings. For novel-state recognition, the reported improvement over the previous state of the art reaches 14.6%, using less than 5% of its inference time. The findings support decomposing states into reusable concepts as a way to improve both recognition transfer and computational efficiency.
neurips-2025-sage-a-unified-framework-fo.tldr: SAGE uses shared language-described state concepts and a refined State-Action Graph to recognize unfamiliar object states efficiently.

paragraphs: This paper studies transformer attention through its Jacobian, which describes how changes to a block's input affect its output. The authors show that this behavior is governed by the query, key, and value projections that define attention. Their analysis connects these familiar components to the mathematical conditioning of the attention block.

Based on that connection, the proposed method systematically changes the spectral properties of each attention layer to reduce the Jacobian's condition number. Conditioning concerns how unevenly a transformation responds to changes in different directions. The intervention therefore targets the sensitivity structure of attention, using the theoretical analysis to guide a modification of the mechanism.

Experiments across multiple transformer architectures and tasks show consistent performance improvements associated with better Jacobian conditioning. The authors describe the method as simple and suitable as a drop-in replacement for a broad range of attention mechanisms. The contribution is both an explanation of what controls attention's conditioning and an empirically validated way to alter it, connecting a mathematical property of individual layers with practical model performance.
neurips-2025-spectral-conditioning-of-at.tldr: The paper improves transformer performance by modifying attention's spectral properties to reduce the condition number of its Jacobian.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to enforce statistical parity while learning decisions in a contextual bandit setting. The goal is to maintain the required parity across groups throughout learning, alongside strong performance guarantees. Its central result guarantees exact statistical parity on every trial, rather than only after averaging over the entire sequence.

The authors construct a meta-algorithm that converts any efficient implementation of Hedge, or equivalently a discrete Bayesian inference algorithm, into an efficient parity-constrained contextual bandit algorithm. Against a comparator subject to the same parity constraint, it achieves the same asymptotic regret bound as the corresponding Exp4 instance run separately for each group. The comparison therefore measures performance relative to alternatives that obey the same fairness requirement.

The paper also handles an unknown target parity distribution that must be estimated online. Through online-to-batch conversion, the approach extends to classification, retaining exact statistical parity and providing strong generalization bounds. Together, these results connect an existing family of efficient learning methods with explicit fairness guarantees in both sequential and batch settings.
neurips-2025-statistical-parity-with-exp.tldr: A meta-algorithm enforces exact statistical parity on every contextual-bandit trial while retaining strong regret guarantees, with an extension to classification.

paragraphs: OracleAD detects anomalies in multivariate time series without requiring labeled anomalies. The framework seeks both accurate detection and an interpretable account of which variables depart from normal behavior. It starts by encoding each variable's history into one causal embedding, trained jointly to predict the present value and reconstruct the input window.

Self-attention then projects these embeddings into a shared space to capture relationships among variables. Those relationships arise from the variables' temporal dynamics rather than being treated as fixed. The projected embeddings are aligned with a Stable Latent Structure representing normal relationships. Detection combines prediction error with deviations from this structure, yielding scores at individual time points and for individual variables.

The authors explain that structural deviations originate in embeddings that violate the learned temporal causality of normal data. This lets OracleAD identify root-cause variables at the embedding level. Experiments report state-of-the-art results across multiple real-world datasets and evaluation protocols. The approach links anomaly scoring and interpretation through the same learned representation of normal temporal and cross-variable relationships.
neurips-2025-structured-temporal-causali.tldr: OracleAD combines prediction errors with deviations from learned normal relationships to detect time-series anomalies and identify implicated variables.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether reward-model accuracy is enough to predict effective reinforcement learning from human feedback. A reward model supplies the training signal for a language model, so its usefulness depends on how that signal shapes optimization. The authors analyze this teaching role through the variation in rewards it induces.

They prove that low reward variance produces a flat RLHF objective landscape regardless of reward-model accuracy. Consequently, even a perfectly accurate model can lead to very slow optimization and perform worse as a teacher than a less accurate model inducing higher variance. They also show that a reward model can work well with one language model yet induce low variance and a flat landscape with another.

Experiments using models with up to eight billion parameters support the relationship between accuracy, reward variance, and the speed of reward maximization. The findings establish a limitation of evaluating reward models solely by accuracy or separately from the language models they guide. Sufficient reward variance is needed for efficient optimization, making teacher quality a property of the training interaction as well as the reward model.
neurips-2025-what-makes-a-reward-model-a.tldr: Reward-model accuracy alone does not ensure effective RLHF: low induced reward variance can make optimization extremely slow, even with perfect accuracy.
